title: 06 Foreign Trade Risks & Risk Management - Topic Quiz

questions.text: In which phase does the risk of non-acceptance occur for an exporter, and why is it especially high for custom-made orders?
options: Before delivery, because commodity costs may increase
After delivery, because foreign exchange rates may fluctuate strongly
During delivery, because custom-made goods are very hard to resell if refused
After warranty expiry, because buyers demand free repairs
questions.correctAnswer: During delivery, because custom-made goods are very hard to resell if refused

questions.text: Palfinger AG quotes an order for USD 10,000.00 at 1 EUR = 1 USD. At payment, the USD drops to 0.90 EUR. What is the unhedged outcome?
options: Palfinger receives EUR 9,000.00 and suffers an exchange rate loss of EUR 1,000.00
Palfinger receives EUR 11,000.00 and makes an exchange rate gain of EUR 1,000.00
Palfinger still receives exactly EUR 10,000.00 with no difference
Palfinger receives EUR 9,900.00 and loses EUR 100.00
questions.correctAnswer: Palfinger receives EUR 9,000.00 and suffers an exchange rate loss of EUR 1,000.00

questions.text: Which Austrian institution refinances subsidized export loans via house banks for SMEs, and which does so for large enterprises?
options: OeKB for SMEs and OeGK for large enterprises
Austrian Export Fund (Exportfonds) for SMEs and Oesterreichische Kontrollbank AG (OeKB) for large enterprises
SVS for SMEs and the Chamber of Commerce for large enterprises
The tax office for SMEs and the ICC Paris for large enterprises
questions.correctAnswer: Austrian Export Fund (Exportfonds) for SMEs and Oesterreichische Kontrollbank AG (OeKB) for large enterprises

questions.text: Which contractual tool specifically protects a company against price change risk from rising global commodity prices?
options: A forward exchange contract with the house bank
Market research in the target export country
Marine transport insurance for the sea leg
A price fluctuation clause or cost fluctuation clause in the contract
questions.correctAnswer: A price fluctuation clause or cost fluctuation clause in the contract

questions.text: What is meant by transfer risk in international trade?
options: The danger that cargo is damaged during transshipment at a port
The danger that money cannot be transferred out of the importer's country
The danger that a freight forwarder picks the wrong shipping route
The danger that an exporter uses unsuitable transport packaging
questions.correctAnswer: The danger that money cannot be transferred out of the importer's country

questions.text: Which safeguards protect an importer against delivery and performance risk (wrong quality, wrong quantity, or delay)?
options: High payment in advance and invoicing in foreign currency
Export financing through the Export Fund and local market research
Omitting Incoterms and paying in full before production begins
Low down payment, credit purchase, contractual penalty, test certificate, and bank guarantee
questions.correctAnswer: Low down payment, credit purchase, contractual penalty, test certificate, and bank guarantee

questions.text: Tridonic delivers LED lighting from Austria to AC Milan in Italy. Which risk is fundamentally eliminated in this export deal?
options: Exchange rate risk, because both countries use the euro
Transport risk, because cargo damage does not occur within the EU
Default risk, because Italian clubs are state-guaranteed
Warranty risk, because defect liability does not apply inside the EU
questions.correctAnswer: Exchange rate risk, because both countries use the euro

questions.text: With a forward exchange contract, an exporter can lock in the exchange rate for a future foreign-currency payment in advance.
There is no difference between a down payment and payment in advance, because both require paying the full purchase price upfront.
Explain the classic conflict of interest between exporter and importer regarding payment terms and name the payment method that balances both sides.
questions.correctAnswer: The exporter prefers a high down payment or full payment in advance to minimize production, non-acceptance, and default risks. The importer prefers a low down payment and credit purchase (paying after delivery) to reduce delivery risk and avoid tying up liquidity. A Letter of Credit balances both interests because the importer's bank pays only upon timely presentation of contract-compliant shipping documents.
